headline: Ordained residential kitchen ordinance effective January 1, 2027; adopted solid waste and stabilization fund orders; referred Malden River Works fund transfers to Finance Committee.
summary: Adopted orders creating a solid waste enterprise fund and two stabilization funds, and sent related ordinances to joint committee sessions. Sent a $266,174.60 appropriation, a $400,000 school transfer, and two Roosevelt Park fund transfers to the Finance Committee. Ordained a residential kitchen ordinance and granted several livery and parking petitions.
decisions: Approved the Consent Agenda by unanimous vote.
Approved the minutes of the September 8, 2026 meeting.
Referred livery company petition 380-26 for Ana Santos Transport, LLC at 64 Linwood Street to the License Committee.
Referred livery driver petition 381-26 for Ana Raque Dias Dos Santos to the License Committee.
Referred the appointment of Michele Ferguson, 43 Boston Street, to the Planning Board to the Personnel/Appointments Committee, by unanimous vote.
Confirmed the reappointment of Lisa Picardi, 18 Phillips Street, to the Disability Commission, by a 9 yes vote.
Adopted order 384-26 to establish a Solid Waste Enterprise Fund beginning with fiscal year FY2028, by unanimous vote.
Referred ordinance 385-26, adding section 3.05 Solid Waste Enterprise Fund, to a joint session of Rules & Ordinance with Finance Committees, by unanimous vote.
Adopted order 386-26 to establish a General Purpose Stabilization Fund, by unanimous vote.
Adopted order 387-26 to establish a Short-Term Capital Needs Special Purpose Stabilization Fund, by unanimous vote.
Referred ordinance 388-26, adding section 3.10 Reserve and Stabilization Fund Framework, to a joint session of Rules & Ordinance with Finance Committees, by unanimous vote.
Adopted order 389-26 ratifying the 2008 adoption of water and sewer collection, abatement, appeal, and lien options, by unanimous vote.
Enrolled ordinance 390-26, changing the water bill inspection requirement from once each year to monthly, by a 10 yes vote.
Referred order 391-26, appropriating $266,174.60 from the TNC Surcharge Municipal Distribution Account, to the Finance Committee, by unanimous vote.
Referred order 392-26, transferring $400,000 from Human Resources Group Insurance Miscellaneous to the Malden Public School Department, to the Finance Committee, by unanimous vote.
Referred order 393-26, repurposing $1,292,045.00 from the Roosevelt Park Revitalization Project to the Malden River Works Project, to the Finance Committee, by unanimous vote.
Referred order 394-26, transferring $938,174.50 from the Roosevelt Park Revitalization Project to the Malden River Works Project, to the Finance Committee, by unanimous vote.
Ordained ordinance 395-26, adding 'or their designee' after Chief of Police for the Transportation Commission, by a 9 yes vote.
Ordained ordinance 396-26, requiring Cannabis Licensing and Enforcement Commission approval before a marijuana establishment license transfer, by a 9 yes vote.
Passed resolution 397-26 urging the state to protect and strengthen the Mass Save program and clean energy grants, by unanimous vote.
Passed resolution 398-26 on working with community partners on rules and programs for micromobility devices, by unanimous vote.
Ordained ordinance 263-26 amending Title 12 on residential kitchens, with an effective date of January 1, 2027, by 8 yes votes and 1 abstention (Winslow).
Granted livery and extended hours petition 354-26 for LeGarde, LLC dba Big Daddy Doggie Daycare at 10 Maplewood Street, by unanimous vote.
Granted livery company petition 355-26 for Kuda's Premium Limo at 244 Kennedy Drive, Apt. 103, by unanimous vote.
Granted livery driver petition 356-26 for Kudakwashg Kachere, by unanimous vote.
Granted livery company petition 357-26 for AKLuxury Transport. LLC at 252 Kennedy Drive, Apt. 612, by unanimous vote.
Granted livery driver petition 358-26 for Aboubacar Koulibaly, by unanimous vote.
Granted outdoor parking petition 359-26 for Melrose Storage Facility, LLC at 235 Washington Street for 72 spaces, by unanimous vote.
Granted outdoor parking renewal petition 360-26 for Three C Realty Trust at 54 Winter Street for 22 spaces, by unanimous vote.
Confirmed the appointment of Julianne King, 29 Sterling Street, to the Council on Aging, by a 9 yes vote.
Confirmed the appointment of Arbin Timilsina, 8 Ingleside Avenue, to the Commission on Climate Action and Sustainability, by a 9 yes vote.

Council President Amanda Linehan · Councillor at Large Karen Colon Hayes · Councillor Paul Condon · Councillor Peg Crowe · Councillor at Large Michelle Luong · Councillor at Large Carey McDonald · Councillor Ryan O'Malley · Councillor Jadeane Sica · Councillor Chris Simonelli · Councillor Ari Taylor · Councillor Stephen Winslow

Tuesday, September 22, 2026 · 7:00 PM · City Council Chambers · 215 Pleasant Street · Malden, MA 02148 · Watch the meeting with Teams: https://tinyurl.com/rtp3pzpt

## 1. CALL TO ORDER

Council President Linehan called the meeting to order at 7:05 PM.

## 2. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE & MOMENT OF SILENCE IN HONOR OF SERVICE MEMBERS

Councillor Condon presented an additional moment of silence in honor of Dr. John Tramondozzi, a lifelong resident of Malden, born in 1942 in the Edgeworth neighborhood. Dr. Tramodozzi served as a Malden Public Library Trustee and President as well as holding leadership positions with both the Malden Historical Commission and the Malden Historical Society.

## 3. ROLL CALL

Present - Councillors: 10 - Karen Colon Hayes, Paul Condon, Peg Crowe, Amanda Linehan, Carey McDonald, Ryan O'Malley, Chris Simonelli, Ari Taylor, Stephen Winslow and Michelle Luong

Absent - Councillors: 1 - Jadeane Sica

## 5. PUBLIC COMMENT

No members of the public were in attendance for public comment.

## 8. MOTIONS, ORDERS, AND RESOLUTIONS

**384-26** 

Order: That the Malden City Council, pursuant to the authority granted under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 44, Section 53F½, hereby adopts the local option to establish a Solid Waste Enterprise Fund beginning with the fiscal year FY2028 for the purpose of separately accounting for the revenues, expenditures, assets, liabilities, and retained earnings associated with the City's solid waste management program.

Sponsors: Stephen Winslow, Karen Colon Hayes, Carey McDonald and Ryan O'Malley

In past discussions related to deficits for solid waste funding, the Council had called for consideration of setting up a solid waste enterprise fund. The purpose of doing so will allow the city to be better able to track revenues and expenditures associated with waste disposal in the city utilizing separate accounting practices. Adopting this order is to adopt the local option within MGL to establish the fund.

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor Simonelli, that the Order be adopted. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**385-26** 

Be it ordained by the Malden City Council that the Code of the City of Malden (MCC) Title 3 REVENUE AND FINANCE is hereby amended by adding 3.05 SOLID WASTE ENTERPRISE FUND

Sponsors: Stephen Winslow, Karen Colon Hayes, Carey McDonald and Ryan O'Malley

With the adoption of Paper 384-26 to establish a solid waste enterprise fund, the Code of the City of Malden must be brought up to date with the creation of procedures which are outlined in the draft of this proposed ordinance paper.

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor O'Malley, that the Ordinance be referred a joint session of Rules & Ordinance with Finance Committees. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**386-26** 

Order: That the Malden City Council, pursuant to the authority granted under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 5B, hereby adopts the local option to establish a General Purpose Stabilization Fund.

Sponsors: Amanda Linehan, Ryan O'Malley and Stephen Winslow

Saving multipurpose sinking funds in the same operating accounts can cause some difficulty when pulling apart reserve balances for differing earmarks. The state has created a framework to manage multiple stabilization funds. Adopting this order is to adopt the local option within MGL that allows for the establishment of general purpose and special purpose stabilization funds.

A motion was made by Councillor McDonald, seconded by Councillor Simonelli, that the Order be adopted. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**387-26** 

Order: That the Malden City Council, pursuant to the authority granted under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 5B, hereby adopts the local option to establish a Short-Term Capital Needs Special Purpose Stabilization Fund.

Sponsors: Amanda Linehan, Ryan O'Malley and Stephen Winslow

Saving multipurpose sinking funds in the same operating accounts can cause some difficulty when pulling apart reserve balances for differing earmarks. The state has created a framework to manage multiple stabilization funds. Adopting this order is to adopt the local option within MGL that allows for the establishment of general purpose and special purpose stabilization funds.

A motion was made by Councillor Simonelli, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Order be adopted. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**388-26** 

Be it ordained by the Malden City Council that the Code of the City of Malden (MCC) Title 3 REVENUE AND FINANCE is hereby amended by adding 3.10 RESERVE AND STABILIZATION FUND FRAMEWORK

Sponsors: Amanda Linehan, Carey McDonald, Ryan O'Malley and Stephen Winslow

With the adoption of Papers 386 & 387-26 to establish stabilization funds, the Code of the City of Malden must be brought up to date with the creation of procedures which are outlined in the draft of this proposed ordinance paper.

Councillor Linehan stated her desire to see this local option with updated ordinance followed by a debt use policy paper outlining models of how decisions are made relative to bonding versus funding projects with existing monies.

A motion was made by Councillor O'Malley, seconded by Councillor Winslow, that the Ordinance be referred to a joint session of Rules & Ordinance with Finance Committees. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**389-26** 

Order: That the Malden City Council, pursuant to the authority granted under Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, hereby ratifies the Public Works Commission’s 2008 adoption of the local options of Sections 42A through 42F, as they pertain to Water/Sewer collection, abatement, appeal, and liens. In conjunction with said sections, a record of Certificate of Acceptance shall be filed with the Middlesex South Registry of Deed and certified copies of the recorded certificate shall be issued to the Treasurer/Collector, Department of Public Works Water Division, and any other relevant City departments.

Sponsors: Carey McDonald and Stephen Winslow

In 2008 The Public Works Commission adopted the local option of M.G.L. c. 40, s. 42A-F but it does not appear that action was properly authorized or registered with the Registry of Deeds. The purpose of this paper is to administratively correct that process and bring Malden's water billing procedures up to date.

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor Colon Hayes, that the Order be adopted. The motion carried by a unanimous vote.

**390-26** 

Be it ordained by the Malden City Council that the Code of the City of Malden (MCC)

11.20.030(A) WATER BILLS; ANNUAL INSPECTION OF PREMISES is hereby amended by striking ‘at least once each year’ and replaced with ‘monthly’.

Sponsors: Stephen Winslow and Carey McDonald

With the adoption of Paper 389-26 to adopt the local option of M.G.L. c. 40, s. 42A-F as they pertain to water/sewer collections, the Code of the City of Malden must be brought up to date with an amendment to the ordinance regulating the billing cycle. It was the general consensus of the body that since the city switched from quarterly to monthly billing in 2008, there was no need to send the amendment through committee. The ordinance was enrolled on the floor.

A motion was made by Councillor Winslow, seconded by Councillor Taylor, that the Ordinance be enrolled. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yea: 10 - Colon Hayes, Condon, Crowe, Linehan, McDonald, O'Malley, Simonelli, Taylor, Winslow and Luong

Councillor Winslow opened discussion on this paper stating he does not think it ready to be ordained as the Board of Health still has to put regulations and practices in place that will coincide with this ordinance. Despite being generally in favor of the overall concept, he will be abstaining from this vote.

The City Clerk reminded the body that this paper was amended on September 8 to reflect an effective date of January 1, 2027 to allow the Board of Health to establish the regulations necessary for inspections and oversight. Councillor Luong noted the city must adopt the MA State Regulations for cottage kitchens, saving the Board of Health from having to write their own policy from scratch.

Councillor Simonelli was not present in the Chamber at the time this vote was taken.
